citations.quote: only when such LC is not acting as a Transfer Agent
Would activities that an RA 13 depositary performs in its capacity as a Transfer Agent (TA) (eg, processing payments in designated accounts) be subject to requirements under the CMR?

In such cases, the depositary is expected to observe relevant requirements under Schedule 11 to the Code of Conduct for Persons Licensed by or Registered with the Securities and Futures Commission (Schedule 11), in particular paragraphs 9 (relating to how subscription and redemption proceeds should be held) and 11 (relating to distribution proceeds).

readings.distinction: The negation attaches to “acting as a Transfer Agent”, and “only when” qualifies the applicability proposition. The preferred contextual reading tests capacity in the relevant activity, supported by Q1's express focus on activities performed in that capacity. Neither “not” nor “only” negates the scheme-money or Hong Kong conditions. Schedule 11 expectations remain separate.

citations.quote: The CMR will apply to an RA 13 licensed corporation (LC) and its associated entity (AE) in respect of “scheme money” received or held in Hong Kong by the RA 13 LC or its AE in the course of conducting Type 13 regulated activity by the RA 13 LC, only when such LC is not acting as a Transfer Agent.

readings.distinction: This rival retains the same local negation but gives the LC's activity a broader domain: any contemporaneous transfer-agent activity defeats the condition for both LC and AE funds. The absence of an express “in respect of that money” restriction makes this grammatically possible, although Q1's activity-specific wording favors the first reading.

vocabulary_concerns: transfer_agent has no activity, funds or time index. The first encoding assumes a transaction-specific assessment; the supplied vocabulary cannot independently distinguish that assessment from corporation-wide concurrent activity.
ra13_context bundles the LC, AE and course-of-activity conditions, preventing separate tests of their relationships.

The vocabulary contains no Schedule 11 duty predicates. Failure of the selected antecedent cannot establish absence of continuing duties, and u19 does not expressly resolve Schedule 11's treatment of every transfer-agent case.
